decisions.executionNote: Raise and incline right gripper toward the mouse, using a gradual elbow-up approach; left arm remains parked.
Advance right wrist above mouse while rotating gripper toward a downward grasp; maintain open fingers.
Lower open right fingers around the mouse with a small lateral correction; depth is estimated from RGB.
Finish the mouse approach and close the right gripper; retention will be checked visually after a small lift.
Lift the closed right gripper and begin transporting the mouse toward the pad, checking whether it stays between the fingers.
Mouse stayed on the table. Return with open fingers and approach about three centimeters lower for a deeper grasp.
Close around the centered mouse at the deeper approach, then lift vertically to test retention before transporting.
Mouse appears retained after the lift. Carry it rightward over the center of the pad, keeping the gripper closed.
Lower the retained mouse onto the pad, open the gripper, and lift slightly clear.
Retract from the placed mouse and raise both wrists into separate approach lanes for a two-sided keyboard push.
Bring closed grippers to separate points behind the keyboard, lowering gradually while keeping elbows in the same configuration.
Lower both closed fingertips just behind the keyboard's front edge before applying an even forward push.
Push the keyboard forward and slightly right with both fingertips, lifting a few millimeters to avoid scraping the table.
Continue the even keyboard push toward the outlined frame, keeping each arm on its own side.
Keyboard visually overlaps its frame. Open both grippers and withdraw; move left toward the figurine while right clears the work area.
Align the left open gripper over the figurine's body and lower cautiously. Return the right wrist toward its starting pose.
Correct toward the figurine's green stem and close gently after a short descent; its base has tilted, so retention is uncertain.
Lift the closed left gripper vertically to verify whether the tilted figurine is retained before moving toward its stand.
Move the raised left gripper toward the stand area while checking whether the figurine follows; avoid the clock and keyboard.
Figurine was not retained. Clear the stand area by approaching the alarm clock from above with the left gripper open.
Lower the left gripper around the clock's upper casing and close; check capture with a subsequent vertical lift.
Maintain closure on the clock, then make a vertical test lift before attempting transport.
Clock was not retained. Reorient the open gripper across its thinner dimension and make a lower approach.
Center the clock within the wrist view, descend slightly, close around the casing, and test with a small lift.
Clock now appears seated between the fingers. Lift vertically with closure maintained before moving across the drawer's edge.
Transport the visibly retained clock upward and left toward the drawer top, preserving the grasp and elbow configuration.
Replan after continuity rejection: smaller upward and forward increments toward the drawer, keeping the clock closed in the gripper.
Reduce motion to millimeter increments to preserve joint continuity near the current folded reach; retain the clock.
Change to a shallower wrist inclination before further transport to avoid the near-limit elbow configuration; keep the clock grasp closed.
Use smaller orientation-only increments to move away from the elbow limit without translating the held clock.
Carry the retained clock over the drawer top with a shallow wrist angle and small continuous increments.
Replan from the interrupted pose: shallow the wrist and retract a little to regain joint margin while keeping the clock closed in the gripper.
With joint margin recovered, translate the retained clock left and slightly back over the drawer's top surface.
Set the clock onto the drawer top with a small inward descent, release it, and withdraw without further extending the elbow.
Clock has been released over the drawer. Recover from the continuity stop with a shallower wrist and small inward retreat, keeping fingers open.
Previous recovery was rejected without movement. Try very small orientation-only increments to preserve the current IK branch.
Withdraw the open left gripper from the clock and drawer, regaining comfortable joint range before returning to the displaced figurine.
Approach the fallen figurine's yellow base from above with open fingers, staying in the left workspace and clear of the drawer.
Descend over the centered yellow base for a vertical pinch. The clock has fallen back to the table and will need another placement.
Correct rightward to center the displaced base between the fingers, then lower slightly and close without forcing through the contact.
Test the base pinch with a slow upward lift and a small inward motion, keeping the left gripper closed.
The base slipped free. Recenter leftward and slightly toward the robot, then descend with open fingers for another base pinch.
Close around the now-centered upright base, pause for seating, then lift a short distance to test retention.
The figurine appears retained by its base. Lift and carry inward toward the stand, keeping the gripper closed and clear of the drawer.
Carry the retained figurine toward the stand and begin rotating its sideways base upright, with clearance above the clock.
Translate toward the gray stand and lower gradually; the figurine shifted during rotation, so retain closure and inspect its support before release.
Tracking stopped near the drawer edge. Open and retreat slightly upward and backward while restoring a downward approach; reassess the figurine's location.
The previous command executed nothing. Start with an observed-pose hold and opening, then use millimeter retreat increments to reestablish continuity.
Use a one-millimeter adjustment to bridge the continuity boundary, open, and then retreat slowly from the obstructed area.
Clear the drawer side to the right within the left workspace, turning the open gripper toward the fallen figurine rather than pressing into the drawer.
Approach the visible yellow base from its right side, advancing and descending in small increments with the gripper open.
Stop descending against contact. Close around the visible base rim and test a small upward-right lift away from the drawer.
The last action executed nothing. Use a small continuity-bridging adjustment, then close and lift cautiously without further descent.
Add a small wrist-angle correction to bridge the rejected IK target; if accepted, close and test a short upward-right lift.
The base is ahead of the fingertips, not securely held. Open and approach it with a straighter downward orientation and a rotated pinch axis to clear the drawer side.
Use the head view to correct the fingertip offset: move left and forward toward the base while descending slowly with open jaws.
The approach is obstructed. Withdraw the open gripper rightward and toward the robot with small wrist changes, rather than continue pressing left.
Lift clear before shifting left; previous sideways approaches were contacting the base rather than straddling it.
Move above the base at clearance height before any further descent, using small forward-left increments.
Lower to regain elbow margin while turning the pinch axis front-to-back, reducing the finger's interference with the drawer side.
Angle the fingertips left toward the base while keeping the wrist clear of the drawer, then close across the base.
Test the current base grasp by moving upward and right toward the stand without rotating the figurine.
The base remains obstructed at the drawer side. Release and retract toward the robot while angling the fingertips away from the drawer.
Approach the base from in front of the drawer, correcting leftward while maintaining a front-to-back pinch axis and lowering cautiously.
Close at the current contact depth and lift slowly for a visual retention check; the wrist view is occluded, so avoid further descent.
Neither object followed the lift. Shift to the clock's visible casing, moving left and lower with open fingers to separate it from the figurine.
Make a short alignment correction around the clock casing, close, and test a small lift. The figurine is now clear of the drawer side.
Test clock retention while lifting leftward. Shallow the wrist during the lift to keep elbow margin for reaching over the drawer.
Clock was not retained. Return above it with a fully downward open gripper for a centered, deeper grasp rather than an edge pinch.
The clock lies ahead of the fingertips in the wrist view. Advance the downward gripper while lowering to bring its casing between the open jaws.
The vertical approach is blocked by the drawer. Retract toward the robot and shallow the wrist for a lower frontal approach, keeping the gripper open.
Previous action executed nothing. Bridge toward the preceding target with a small adjustment, then gradually retract and shallow the wrist to clear the drawer.
With the frontal approach clear, lower the open fingers around the clock casing and close at the estimated side-grasp height.
Lift vertically with the clock grasp closed and verify whether the casing follows before attempting another transport.
Clock remained on the table. Recenter slightly left and make a deeper frontal approach so the fingertips reach the casing sides rather than closing above them.
Close on the clock's casing at the deeper approach and lift vertically to check that it remains between the fingers.
Clock now appears retained. Lift leftward in front of the drawer, shallowing the wrist to preserve joint margin before moving over the top.
The clock is retained but still below the drawer rim. Raise it above the top before advancing farther, easing wrist pitch for joint margin.
Clock is now above the drawer surface. Move slightly inward, lower onto the top, and release without lifting against the joint limit.
